St. Louis area interests also support the proposal, but many suggest changes in the population-mileage formula to include an industrial area of western St. Louis County which does not fall within the expanded zone. With regard to Los Angeles, the City of Compton, Calif., which as proposed would be partially within the Los Angeles Harbor zone, urges that it be included in its entirety within the Harbor zone.
The Port Authority of New York and New Jersey generally supports the proposed expansion but seeks changes in the proposed sections 1048.11 and 1048.12. As proposed, section 1048.11(b) would permit export, import, or domestic waterborne cargo moving from marine terminals on the New York City side of the harbor to have the benefit of the 20 mile commercial zone exemption while denying it to cargo moving to or from marine terminals on the New Jersey side of New York harbor. The Port Authority recommends that this situation be corrected by extending the exemption to the New Jersey communities which are within the New York, N. Y., commercial zone. It also urges that sections 1048.11(b) and 1048.12(b) be amended so as to afford the exemption to transportation of goods between those points in New Jersey and between those points in Westchester and Nassau Counties, N.Y., which are within the expanded zone. It argues that unless this is done inefficient operations will result.
